answer: For agents trading pearl and onyx, allocate listing slots through memory-hard puzzles bound to the account key and a fresh epoch nonce. Each accepted solution buys one slot; validators reject reused solutions, and there is no free quota per account. Agents may wander between aliases, but every additional slot still requires fresh computation and memory bandwidth. An attacker running thousands of identities must pay for proportionally more hardware time and electricity, rather than multiplying free listings.
